subject: Helix Therapeutics — onboarding: network preflight & validation plan
messages:
From: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@helixtx.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@helixtx.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helix onboarding — network preflight and questions

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're ready to start the private deployment intake and want to align on the preflight items so there are no surprises during provisioning. Attached is our internal network sketch (network-diagram-v2.png) — it shows our proposed VPC pairs, transit gateway, and where we expect the Redwood enclave to sit.

Can you confirm the minimum required:
- Subnet counts and sizing per AZ for the Redwood enclave
- NAT / EIP expectations for outbound egress and any per-tenant limits
- DNS delegation approach (we can either delegate subdomain to Redwood or use private forwarding)
- Any firewall rules you require inbound for health checks and admin access

Also: we have a procurement cutover the week of 8/23. If we can close the preflight by 8/13 that would be ideal so we can schedule installation for the 8/24 window.

Attaching: network-diagram-v2.png (image/png)

Thanks,
Asha Kapoor
Head of IT — Helix Therapeutics
asha.kapoor@helixtx.com
+1 (415) 555-0108

From: connor.obrien@redwood.com
To: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@helixtx.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Helix onboarding — network preflight and questions

Asha — thanks for the diagram. High level response below and a proposed validation plan. I copied the infra and onboarding folks to validate specifics.

Quick answers (summary):
- Subnets: we recommend 3 subnets per AZ for the Redwood serving layer: control (small), worker (scalable), and kv-cache (if isolated). Minimum sizes: /26 for control, /22 for worker, /27 for kv-cache as a starting point — we can tune based on expected token throughput.
- NAT/EIP: plan for 2x NAT gateways per AZ for redundancy. Per-tenant outbound IPs are allocated via EIP pool — we'll need the final count early. Attached is a CSV template (nat-eip-list.csv) to capture expected fixed egress IPs for integrations (webhooks, partner allowlists).
- DNS: either delegate a subdomain to our private resolver (preferred) or provide a set of conditional forwarders. We'll include concrete steps in the runbook.
- Firewall: allow outbound 443 to our control-plane ranges; inbound only from our maintenance bastion IPs for admin (we'll provide the list). Health checks use 443/https on the service endpoint and a separate metrics port for telemetry — we'll include port numbers in the final doc.

Proposed short validation plan (complete by 8/13):
1) Helix provides subnet CIDRs and EIP needs using nat-eip-list.csv (attached).
2) Redwood validates MTU / routing constraints and confirms required security group rules.
3) CloudTransit (if in path) confirms BGP/peering details and any NAT transits.
4) Joint smoke test: small sample traffic to confirm connectivity and KV cache warm-up.

Next steps for you: fill nat-eip-list.csv and drop back; we'll schedule a 45-minute validation call (suggest 8/12 or 8/13, see calendar link).

Attachments: nat-eip-list.csv

—
Connor O'Brien
Technical Account Lead | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 13:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Helix onboarding — network preflight and questions

Connor / team — a few technical notes to capture before we lock the plan: 

MTU and fragmentation
- If Helix's on-prem edge uses jumbo frames (MTU > 1500), we need to validate path MTU across transit. Default assumption: 1500. Any deviation must be documented; we'll run an MTU probe during the smoke test.

NAT behavior and ephemeral source ports
- Some Helix integrations expect stable source ports; if that's a hard requirement we should consider SNAT with dedicated appliances or explicit port mapping. CloudTransit — can you confirm if your layer supports source-port persistence?

Route propagation and BGP
- If using BGP, advertise only the Helix public prefixes and avoid leaking internal-only CIDRs. We'll provide the minimal AS path expectations but need CloudTransit to confirm the BGP timers they observe.

Firewall and IDS tuning
- For telemetry we recommend a short-lived exception for our health checks from the bastion IPs; IDS teams should whitelist those flows ahead of the smoke test.

I'll pull together a short one-page MTU/firewall note and attach (mtu-and-firewall-notes.pdf).

-karthik
Karthik Iyer 
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: infra@cloudtransit.com
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: rahul.mehta@cloudtransit.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:17:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Helix network preflight / CloudTransit scope

Connor / Karthik — thanks for looping us in. Quick confirmations from CloudTransit: 

- BGP: we support IPv4/IPv6 BGP peering with session MD5 and typical timer defaults (60/180). We'll provide the ASNs and MD5 key exchange via a 1:1 secure channel (do not post in email).
- NAT: we support SNAT with port preservation for most flows; for guaranteed stable source-port mapping we recommend a dedicated SNAT appliance (we can quote).
- Maintenance window: we have a scheduled backbone upgrade on 8/21-8/22 UTC — that is outside the proposed 8/24 installation but worth acknowledging.

We'll attend the validation call and can provide a small config snippet (bgp-peer-template.txt) and ops contact (Rahul Mehta) during the meeting.

Regards,
CloudTransit Operations
infra@cloudtransit.com
Rahul Mehta — Technical Account Manager
rahul.mehta@cloudtransit.com

Subject: Helix network preflight — next steps & validation call (proposed)

Team — summary and concrete asks before the joint validation call: 

Outstanding items for Helix (action items):
1) Complete and return nat-eip-list.csv with expected fixed egress IPs and any upstream allowlists by EOD 8/11 PST (we received a partial copy; please finalize).
2) Confirm whether jumbo frames are used at your edge (yes/no) and provide any MTU constraints.
3) Confirm DNS approach: delegate helix.example.com or provide conditional forwarder IPs.

Redwood / CloudTransit deliverables prior to call:
- Redwood to publish the final port list and control-plane CIDRs (we will send by 8/12 17:00 UTC).
- CloudTransit to share BGP ASN and ops contact (Rahul) in a secure channel.

Validation call (45m) — options: 2026-08-12 17:00 UTC or 2026-08-13 14:00 UTC. Please confirm preferred slot and we'll send a calendar invite.

Links: runbook draft (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cHelix-Onboard-Runbook), proposed invite (https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=helix-network-validation-20260813)

If we can close preflight by 8/13 we can proceed with provisioning the week of 8/24 as requested.

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
